Take $n=2^{p-1}q_1q_2\cdots q_k$ with $p$ a large prime and $q_i$ distinct odd primes for which the odd part of $q_i-1$ is $1$ (Fermat primes) or, more generally, a fixed odd integer $t$. Then
$$d(n)=p\cdot 2^k,\qquad \varphi(d(n))=(p-1)2^{k-1}.$$
Moreover $\varphi(n)=2^{p-2}\prod(q_i-1)$ has the form $2^{A}\cdot t^{k}$ (up to bounded factors), so
$$d(\varphi(n))=(A+1)\,d(t^k)= (p+O_k(1))\cdot O(k).$$
Hence
$$\frac{\varphi(d(n))}{d(\varphi(n))}=\frac{(p-1)2^{k-1}}{p\cdot O(k)}\sim \frac{2^{k-1}}{O(k)}\to\infty$$
as $k\to\infty$ (with $p$ taken sufficiently large relative to $k$). Thus no universal constant $C$ exists.
